# lean-pkg comparator host-check

can this host run the comparator; read-only.

## Usage

```text
lean-pkg comparator host-check [--routes] [--json]
```

## Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--routes` | per route (judge = `lake comparator` in bwrap, prepare = setup stages, transfer = build here, judge elsewhere) supported yes/no with the reason, executables (type -P), locale, open-file limits, CPUs, cgroup memory and a command line per supported route; read-only; exit 0 when any route is supported |

## Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `comparator host-check` | read-only, needs no registry: can this host produce comparator receipts? One `ok`/`warn`/`fail` line each for `kernel`, `landlock` (ABI; below 4 is a `warn`), `bwrap` (user namespace), `go`, `cargo`, `jq`, `git`, `lean`, `lake`, `python3`, then one `mechanism toolchain|legacy: ok|fail` line each against that mechanism's own requirements (toolchain: `bwrap`, `lean`, `lake`, `python3`; legacy: Landlock ABI 1 or later, `go`, `cargo`, `git`, `jq`, `lean`, `lake`), then a verdict naming only the usable mechanisms and saying that Palomar runs only `toolchain`; exit 0 when one is usable, else 1; see [The comparator tier](../comparator.md#checking-a-host-first). `--routes` (run it inside the job's image with the job's binds and `PATH`, before `sbatch`): one `route judge|prepare|transfer: yes|no (reason)` line each with `run:` command lines when supported (judge = `lake comparator` in `bwrap`, never an unsandboxed route; prepare = `lean-pkg receipt comparator --prepare`; transfer = build here, judge on a host with `judge: yes`), then executables resolved like `type -P` (the Slurm template's tools included), locale (a set locale that is not installed is a `warn`), open-file limits with the `LEAN_NUM_THREADS=3` advice when tight, CPUs, cgroup memory limit; additive JSON `routes_schema`, `routes[]`, `executables`, `locale`, `limits`, `resources`, `advice[]`; exit 0 when any route is supported; see [Planning routes before sbatch](../comparator.md#planning-routes-before-sbatch) | `[--routes]` `[--json]` |

## Exit codes

Exit 1 is also a negative answer here:

- `comparator host-check`: this host cannot run the comparator

## JSON output

Top-level keys of `--json`, as recorded in the golden contract (tests/golden/json-keys.json):

- `comparator-host-check` (exit depends on the host): `can`, `checks`, `env_warnings`, `mechanism_detail`, `mechanisms`, `ok`, `palomar`, `verdict`
- `comparator-host-check-routes` (exit depends on the host): `advice`, `can`, `checks`, `env_warnings`, `executables`, `limits`, `locale`, `mechanism_detail`, `mechanisms`, `ok`, `palomar`, `resources`, `routes`, `routes_schema`, `verdict`

## Examples

Can this machine produce comparator receipts? Needs no registry; exit 1 when it cannot.

```bash
lean-pkg comparator host-check
```

Per route (judge here, prepare here, build here and judge elsewhere), whether it is supported and why.

```bash
lean-pkg comparator host-check --routes
```
